desc:
A long strip is painted with several coats. Each coat is a triple [start, end, color] and covers the half-open stretch [start, end). Every coat has a different positive color value. Where coats overlap, the colors mix, and the mixed value is the sum of the colors of all coats covering that stretch.

Collect every distinct start and end coordinate and sort them. Each pair of consecutive coordinates a < b forms a piece [a, b). Return the list [a, b, mixedValue] of all pieces that are covered by at least one coat, in increasing order. Pieces nobody paints are left out.

paints = [[1, 6, 2], [4, 9, 5]]
result = [[1, 4, 2], [4, 6, 7], [6, 9, 5]]

With [[1, 3, 2], [5, 8, 4]] the answer is [[1, 3, 2], [5, 8, 4]]: the piece [3, 5) is unpainted and is skipped.
constraints: 1 ≤ color ≤ 100,000, and all colors are distinct
hints: Only coordinates that are a start or an end of some coat can change the mixed value. There are at most 2 × paints.length of them.
When you walk from left to right, a coat starting adds its color to the running mix and a coat ending removes it.

Store delta[start] += color, delta[end] -= color and a similar +1/-1 coat counter in a dictionary, sort the coordinates, sweep, and output a piece for each pair of neighbouring coordinates while the coat counter is positive.
editorial: This is a difference array over a huge coordinate range, kept sparse. At each coordinate we add the colors of coats that begin there and subtract the colors of coats that end there; the running sum is the mixed value on the piece that follows.

Since every color is at least 1, a sum above zero would already mean 'covered', but we also keep a coat counter so the logic does not depend on that. Sorting the at most 2n coordinates and sweeping them gives O(n log n) time and O(n) space. The largest possible mix is 2,000 distinct colors ≤ 100,000 each, below 2×10<sup>8</sup>.
